statement: In search.py implement lower_bound(a, x), upper_bound(a, x) and count_in_range(a, lo, hi) for a list a of finite numbers sorted in ascending order. lower_bound returns the index of the first element >= x (len(a) if none); upper_bound returns the index of the first element > x (len(a) if none); count_in_range returns how many elements e satisfy lo <= e <= hi (0 when hi < lo). The input is guaranteed sorted and finite: no validation is required.
success_criterion: The three functions return the stated values for every sorted list of finite numbers, and the unit tests pass.
oracles: comparison with a brute-force count on random inputs

submission.claim: search.py implements the three functions as specified; all 9 unit tests pass, including a randomized comparison with brute force.
assertions: lower_bound returns the index of the first element >= x, or len(a)
upper_bound returns the index of the first element > x, or len(a)
count_in_range returns the number of elements in [lo, hi], and 0 when hi < lo
submission.provenance: Two half-open binary searches; count_in_range is upper_bound(hi) - lower_bound(lo). Verified with python3 -m unittest test_search -v, including 2000 random cases against a linear scan.
